sources.reason: ROM initialization source and power-manager material with ROMTools dependency and assembler optimization controls. Sparse documentation; partial reconstruction and build prerequisites must not imply independently verified complete ROM matching.

Pascal/compiler/editor/system sources rebuilt through original tools. Upstream accounts separately for matching file bytes, copied PASCALIO segment, linker slack and disk-image differences; no blanket 100% reconstruction claim.

Historical version4 MASM source explicitly selects CMOS6502; source/platform version nuances retained. Native build uses6502 co-processor and disk tooling; checksum is upstream claim, not independently reproduced.
Original source archive plus build-fixed working sources. Original line endings, comment error and build bugs documented separately; Turbo256K co-processor environment required by supplied workflow.
DFS1.20,NFS3.60 and Tube Host1.10 source package. Upstream explicitly reports two padding-byte differences from released ROM, so a successful source build is not automatically the retail hash.
Historical macro assembler with normal/Turbo co-processor variants. Supplied workflow uses Turbo256K; unpadded Turbo output may have varying hashes and DFS versions are not currently built.

Historical Logica A500 source is an Archimedes adaptation of BBC AIV, not simply the BBC release. Real BCPL lives under build/src/*.b; path rewriting restores build layout, and README notes RISC OS3 linking failure.

Assembly source distinguishes original Atom ROM and BBC sideways-ROM branch with different OS entry points/workspace. No README; actual conditional source and Makefile establish dual target rather than inference from name.

Single-file annotated source with title-image decoder and ZX-M8XXX entry hints. Related SkoolKit presentation is already tracked and linked upstream; retain that relationship, not a claim of wholly independent reversing.

Despite TRS80 repository name, README explicitly says original TRS80 version is not yet present. Actual Apple II BASIC with keyboard PEEK/POKE and machine-code analysis plus mods; no TRS80 target claim.

Historical disk/driver/system sources and revision snapshots. TCS Genie IIIs is distinct from EACA Genie III; preserved source/disk images require external emulator or hardware and are not themselves an emulator.

Address-backed firmware documentation and executable factory-patch decoder. Firmware/patch ROMs are separate; decoder combines byte parameters with external patchbook names. Do not confuse6809 with8031 or claim complete rewrite.

Proof-of-concept banked cartridge with writable first bank and CBIOS/terminal code. Disk access is read-only and requires compatible/modified emulator mapper; not an ordinary unmodified cartridge or hardware-verified port.

Rust crates for character sets,BASIC and SF7000 filesystem access plus dump command. Source modules establish actual data handling despite absent root README; no complete media compatibility measurement.

Address-anchored notes, dispatch entries, generated listing and original-ROM checks. Easy/hard dumps compared separately; physical byte coverage and comment density are not identical semantic-certainty measures. Own ROM required.
ProDOS BASIC.SYSTEM extension for DOS3.3 interoperability with named source. Documented whole-sector loads and overwritten bytes are retained hazards, not silently described as safe file operations.

Resident/overlay listings and extraction/cross-reference tooling behind separate por-go port. No original bytes distributed; scripts use explicit overlay map. Workbench is not the native Go engine itself.

Named68000 module source, ROM/RAM maps and byte-comparison workflow. Repository description says static recompilation but delivered goal/source is assembly reassembly. Complete naming and semantic-quality claims not independently audited.

Partially split object/music/level source with genuine Jaws enemy logic and substantial remaining binary chunks. Claimed matching build does not mean complete source recovery; overflows can break build.
Palette conversion/editor with explicit5-bit RGB and dark-bit representation plus palette/export formats. Small source-backed tool, not broad graphics conversion or verified hardware colour matching.
Table-driven text-to-hex and single/double-byte relative-search utilities. Supports translation investigation; not a complete translation patch or game reconstruction.

CROM/SROM tile conversion and integration-code generation with palette/deduplication/layout rules. README credits city41 upstream, now unavailable in this check; preserved implementation does not imply this mirror is canonical maintainer.

Annotated game routines, tile/string names and Mesen tooling. Large source inspected from pinned read-only Git checkout after connector returned empty content. US matching/completeness claims remain upstream-only.
Actual ROM disassembler and hint parser hardcode Tetris cartridge assumptions and memory layout. Early focused analysis tool, not a general NES disassembler or complete Tetris reconstruction.

Browser-local disc/model/texture/code exploration augmented by game decomp maps. ADX decoder explicitly excludes AHX; raw-disc features and decomp-assisted assembled animation differ. No game assets supplied.

decisions.reason: Expression/parser code produces DASM assembly for a deliberately modified C subset. Not a standards-complete C compiler; platform scripts may need path fixes.

decisions.title: Atalan retargetable 8-bit compiler
decisions.reason: Preserved/updated rule-driven compiler with actual basic-block optimization. Original author Rudla/Rudolf Kudla credited; abandoned origins, bugs and documentation drift explicit, not a polished maintained compiler claim.

decisions.title: LZSA compression and 8-bit decoders
decisions.reason: Byte-aligned formats,host compressor and architecture-specific decoders. Raw/stream and forward/backward variants require correct pairing; performance comparisons remain upstream workload-specific.

decisions.title: Daniel Dallmann opt65 peephole optimizer
decisions.reason: Historical optimizer v0.12 with Ralph Moeritz modifications. Original freeware/non-sale notice retained; not automatically unrestricted open-source licensing or proven semantic safety.

decisions.title: reasm Motorola 68000 assembler
decisions.reason: reasm-core-based assembler with concrete ADD/SUB addressing-form implementation. Dependency and supported instruction-family boundaries remain explicit; no build or complete-ISA claim tested.

decisions.title: Easier68k assembler and simulator
decisions.reason: Archived student-origin project with actual opcode assembly/execution code. Incomplete ISA/floating-point and accurate cycle measurement remain missing; not an accurate full-machine emulator.

decisions.title: ResKnife Macintosh resource editor
decisions.reason: Historical Classic/Carbon and separate Cocoa implementations. README describes incomplete pre-release editor and recommends copies of files; source availability does not establish current macOS compatibility or safe editing.

decisions.title: extract-adf Amiga OFS recovery
decisions.reason: Recovers files from broken OFS ADF/ADZ/DMS media with timestamps. FFS unsupported; invalid end-sector can trigger bus error. Read-only code review, no user disks accessed.

decisions.title: Rust PFS3 filesystem tools
decisions.reason: PFS3 rootblock/anode parser plus read/write/check/FUSE tools for images and devices. Host filesystem implementation distinct from original Amiga driver; write/repair safety not independently tested or exercised.

decisions.title: The Hobbit SC-3000 empty repository
decisions.reason: Description advertises an AI SC-3000 port, but repository metadata has size 0 and commits/main returns 409 Git Repository is empty. Preserve as lead, not an implemented port.

notes: Parent-only pass across 36 platform/type search lanes and 345 distinct search results. Thirty-nine additions and one empty-repository deferral. Pinned primary source and README inspected after current catalogue/prior-decision screening. Historical release source, later platform adaptations, p-code/compiler reconstruction and binary-copy/linker-slack exceptions kept separate. TRS80-named Taipan source correctly assigned Apple II; Domesday A500 code correctly identified as Archimedes adaptation. Historical MASM/BCPL/BASIC files inspected despite unusual or absent extensions and build directory names. Large Milon source returned empty through connector, so read-only shallow Git retrieval inspected the exact pinned commit; no candidate code built or executed. Source attribution and related SkoolKit/Go-port work retained. Empty SC-3000 Hobbit description not promoted as code. Format limits, incomplete emulation/assembler ISA, licensing notices and data-loss warnings preserved.
